answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond before trading, with the bond slashed for proven fraud. Like water carving karst slowly, trust then accumulates only through a long history of completed, peer-attested work, not instant claims. A newcomer may wander the ocean of open tasks freely, but high-value deals require bonded history, so an attacker must pay a bond and wait for every fake identity, making mass fakery expensive and slow.
